subject: Coupa vendor activation: signer authorization, tax-id exception & EDI note
messages:
From: Lisa Tran <lisa.tran@medequip.io>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement Ops <procurement@medequip.io>
Date: Mon, 09 Apr 2028 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Coupa vendor activation – signer matrix & tax-id exception

Hi Irene,

Thanks for kicking off the vendor activation for MedEquip. We started the Coupa enrollment but ran into two items that need Redwood legal/finance confirmation before we can complete the portal registration: 

1) Signer authorization: Our vendor portal requires a signed signer matrix that lists who can accept the order form on behalf of the vendor (two-tier: legal & finance). We uploaded a blank template (attached Signer_Matrix_Request.pdf).

2) Tax ID exception: MedEquip operates under a separate tax entity for certain medical divisions and are requesting an exception to associate PO payments to the divisional EIN rather than the parent. They provided a TaxID_Exception_Form (attached).

Also, quick EDI question — our EDI team flagged a remark field requirement for PO line notes (they expect a two-character qualifier in the REF segment): see EDI_Remark_Specs_v1.xlsx. Can you confirm whether Redwood requires any specific PO acknowledgment window or PO line format before we finish enrollment?

Goal is to go-live in Coupa this month if we can close these three items.

Appreciate a quick playbook of next steps and any docs you need from us.

Thanks,
Lisa Tran
Sr. Procurement Manager
MedEquip Solutions
attachments: Signer_Matrix_Request.pdf, TaxID_Exception_Form.docx, EDI_Remark_Specs_v1.xlsx

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: Lisa Tran <lisa.tran@medequip.io>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 09 Apr 2028 10:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Coupa vendor activation – signer matrix & tax-id exception

Lisa — thanks for the clear summary and for attaching everything. I looped in Kim from Legal and Jonas from Platform Ops so we can triage the three items. High-level next steps from our side: 

- Signer matrix: Legal needs to confirm who on your template is authorized. Kim, can you review the Signer_Matrix_Request.pdf and confirm which signature tier we accept on the order form? If anything needs to be tightened (e.g., block delegation, PO acceptance language), call it out.

- Tax ID exception: Finance (Jonas) will validate whether we can map payments to a divisional EIN without changing the vendor master. Jonas — do we need additional evidence (W9, incorporation docs) to authorize exceptions? If allowed, we'll record an exception in the Coupa vendor profile and flag the payment routing.

- EDI remark field: Platform Ops needs to confirm our PO generator can populate the REF qualifier you mentioned. Jonas — can you confirm the REF/PO remark mapping and whether it impacts our EDI ISA/GS envelope config. If it does, we may need an EDI change request (low-risk).

I can assemble a short mutual action plan for enrollment once we have the legal/finance confirmation. If you have a preferred signer for the DocuSign flow, attach the name and email and we’ll send the DocuSign for the signer matrix.

Irene Choi
Manager, Strategic Procurement Partnerships
Redwood Inference
attachments: (none)

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Lisa Tran <lisa.tran@medequip.io>
Date: Mon, 09 Apr 2028 14:18:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Coupa vendor activation – signer matrix & tax-id exception

Irene / team — reviewed the signer matrix and tax-id form. Key items / redlines below (attaching short redline and the TaxID review checklist):

1) Signer authorization: Recommend we accept single-signature for finance-only POs up to $50k, but legal-level contract/Order Form acceptance requires one of the individuals listed in the legal column. On the template, add explicit language: "Authorized signers may not delegate signature authority without prior written consent from Redwood". I attached Signer_Matrix_Redline.pdf (stub).

2) Tax ID exception: We can accept a divisional EIN mapping for payment routing only if MedEquip provides:
   - W9 for the division (or equivalent foreign tax form)
   - Evidence of the division's bank account ownership or a signed payment routing addendum
If those docs are provided, Finance will create an exception flag in the vendor master (Coupa) and add the alternate EIN in the payment instructions. See TaxID_Exception_Form.docx redline (attached).

3) EDI remark field: The REF qualifier is fine but we need to validate that the qualifier is idempotent across inbound PO acknowledgements. Jonas, if the REF usage changes the Purchase Order XML namespace or line item schema we might need a short EDI mapping change. Prefer to handle this as a Coupa mapping (no model/code changes), but need Ops confirmation.

4) PO acknowledgement window: Standard Redwood terms are 48 hours to acknowledge; if MedEquip needs >48 hours for initial enrollment that’s OK but call it out in the Coupa notes so SRE/order routing can tolerate the delay.

Once MedEquip returns the completed signer matrix and W9 + bank proof, we can finalize the Coupa vendor profile and issue the DocuSign order form for legal signature.

Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Commercial Contracts
Redwood Inference
attachments: Signer_Matrix_Redline.pdf, TaxID_Exception_Form_Redline.docx

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: Lisa Tran <lisa.tran@medequip.io>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Apr 2028 15:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Coupa activation next steps + DocuSign link

Lisa — thanks for the quick turnaround. Per Kim and Jonas below, next steps to complete Coupa enrollment and get your vendor activated: 

Action items for MedEquip (please return items 1–3 to procurement@medequip.io and cc procurement@redwood.com):
1) Completed Signer Matrix (use attached Signer_Matrix_Request.pdf) with the designated legal and finance signers filled in.
2) W9 (or equivalent) for the division + bank account proof for payment routing (required for Tax ID exception).
3) Confirm preferred signer email for DocuSign flow (legal-level signer for Order Form).

What we’ll do:
- Legal will apply minor redlines to the signer matrix (see attached Signer_Matrix_Redline.pdf).
- Finance will prepare the vendor master exception for the alternate EIN once we have W9 + bank proof.
- Platform Ops will update the Coupa vendor profile and add the REF qualifier mapping — minimal impact expected.

DocuSign link (prepped for legal-level signer after we receive completed matrix): https://docusign.example.com/prepare/MEQ-2028-041

If you can get the documents back by EOD Friday 2028-04-13 we’ll aim to have Coupa active by 2028-04-18 and enable PO routing for your first test order.

Thanks again — looping in procurement@redwood.com for tracking.

Irene Choi
Manager, Strategic Procurement Partnerships
Redwood Inference
